evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires nonzero, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. A guest reboot between the `manager.before` and `manager.after` observations can produce a new manager PID and invocation ID on a different boot, so the check can pass even though the manager snapshots span a reboot. The separate `boot_id_changed` check compares only the later reboot snapshots and does not cover the manager phase. Requiring a nonempty, equal boot ID in both manager snapshots while retaining the PID and invocation checks fixes the false-positive path.
